newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two bids in for big Russian SIDANKO oil firm stake.
newsitem.headline: Two bids in for big Russian SIDANKO oil firm stake.

text.p: Two bids have been received for a 51 percent stake in Russian oil company SIDANKO which is being auctioned in an investment tender on Friday, the secretary of the tender commission said on Thursday.
She declined to say from whom the bids had been received. Bids had to be placed by 11 a.m. Moscow time (0800 GMT) on Thursday and the results will be known at around 12 noon (0900) on Friday.
Russia's Federal Property Fund is offering 118.53 million shares in SIDANKO at a starting price of $129 million.

OAO Sibirsko-Dalnevostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (SIDANKO) is one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil groups created over the last few years. Its main operating units are Chernogorneft, Kondpetroleum and Varyoganneftegaz.

The stake for sale is currently managed by MFK Bank, which is associated with Uneximbank (Oneksimbank in Russian), which won control of the shares under the government's shares-for-loans programme in December 1995 in return for a $130 million loan.
In September last year Interros Oil, affiliated with the Interros financial-industrial group built around Uneximbank, won an investment tender for 34 percent of SIDANKO.
The oil company said at the end of December that it planned to issue convertible bonds and treble its authorised capital as part of a plan to consolidate shares of its subsidiaries into the parent.
It also is currently caught up in an ownership dispute over Purneftegaz with state-controlled Rosneft.

The winner of the tender must transfer within one month a further $100 million to SIDANKO to finance the development of oil exploration and production activities, and transfer a further $61 million within a year for the financial stabilisation of SIDANKO.
It must also transfer to SIDANKO 73.70 million shares in the Angara refinery, in which SIDANKO already owns 38 percent, or 51 percent of the voting shares.
